E
Elżbieta – Poland
September 30, 2026 - Verified booking

The activity was well organised and we had the best time visiting the breathtaking sites in Atacama and Salar de Uyuni! A few tips for everyone considering this activity: our drivers only spoke Spanish, so I'd recommend having offline translation downloaded; there is no signal during this tour so make sure to have all important things accessible offline; there is no heating in the accommodation and the temperatures dropped to as low as -8 during our tour so thermal clothes/hat/gloves/winter jacket were a non-negotiable; waiting at the border of Chile/Bolivia took us 4 hours so be prepared for a long wait; in Bolivia you need to present a filled declaration (check online) - it only worked on Android phone and wifi was a struggle so fill it in advance; altitude on day 1 reaches 5k meters so I recommend having at least one day to acclimatise before starting the tour; luggage is carried on top of the car so backpack is recommended.

Lasse – Germany
September 18, 2026 - Verified booking

I must say, our guide, Jonathan, carried the whole experience. He was truly amazing and made this cool experience possible. The accommodation on the first night, however, is very rough. I was freezing the whole night as they don’t provide any heating whatsoever. Also, they didn’t want to provide me a towel at first and the bedsheets were unfortunately stained and with hairs. Apart from that, the nature of Bolivia is truly stunning and made all the hardships of the first night worthwhile. Our guide cooked excellent meals during the days, drove safely, and explained us a lot about the different spots we visited. Without Jonathan, this experience would have been very different. Thanks again Jonathan.

Highlights
Journey from the driest desert to the world's largest salt flat.
See vibrant Laguna Verde and the surreal Salvador Dalí Desert.
Soak in hot springs with flamingos, capture sunrise photos at Incahuasi Island.
Explore the vast Salar de Uyuni, creating unique and unforgettable memories.
This tour showcases Earth's most extraordinary natural wonders.
Full description
Day 1
Departure and Immigration:
Your adventure begins with an early morning pick-up from your hostel in San Pedro de Atacama. In a comfortable Mercedes Benz van, we will ascend 2,000 meters in 45 minutes, crossing the Chilean and Bolivian borders after a hearty breakfast.

Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde:
Our first stops are the mesmerizing Laguna Blanca and Laguna Verde. Admire the striking colors of these high-altitude lakes, surrounded by sacred volcanoes, and capture incredible photos.

Desert and Hot Springs:
Next, we visit the Salvador Dalí Desert, where the surreal landscapes inspire awe and make for great photo opportunities. Enjoy a relaxing dip in the Polques Hot Springs, where you can soak in warm waters while watching flamingos.

Geysers and Laguna Colorada:
Afterwards, we head to the Geyser del Sol de la Mañana, located at nearly 5,000 meters above sea level. Marvel at the fumaroles and eruptions in this otherworldly location. Our day concludes at Laguna Colorada, home to Andean flamingos, set in the stunning Eduardo Abaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve.

Overnight in Quetena Chico:
We'll have dinner and spend the night at a cozy hostel in the remote village of Quetena Chico.

Day 2
Valley of Rocks and Unique Formations:
Following breakfast, we journey north to the Valley of Rocks. Here, you’ll see fascinating formations like the Camel Rock and the Stone Tree, known for their unusual shapes sculpted by wind and time.

Laguna Catal and Gorge:
Our next stop is Laguna Catal, where you can explore the gorge and observe native Bolivian flora and fauna. Take in the serene landscapes and snap photos, then enjoy a delicious lunch.

Salt Hostel Stay:
The day ends with a restful evening at the famous salt hotel, where you'll enjoy dinner and prepare for the next day's wonders.

Day 3
Salar de Uyuni Adventure:
We depart early to the Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat. Experience the vast white expanse that stretches over 10,000 square kilometers.

Incahuasi Island Sunrise:
Arrive at Incahuasi Island for an unforgettable sunrise amidst ancient cacti. This elevated spot offers panoramic views of the salt flat.

Photo Opportunities:
On the salt flats, unleash your creativity with perspective photos using props. Visit the salt hotel and the Plaza de las Banderas, then marvel at the Ojos del Salar, where volcanic bubbles emerge in vibrant hues.

Colchani Village and Train Cemetery:
In Colchani, shop for unique souvenirs before visiting the Train Cemetery in Uyuni. This eerie yet fascinating site showcases Bolivia's industrial past.

Return to Quetena Chico:
After lunch at a local restaurant, we head back to our agency in Uyuni for customs formalities, then return to Quetena Chico for another restful night.

Day 4
Return to San Pedro de Atacama:
Following breakfast, we begin our journey back to San Pedro de Atacama, where you'll be dropped off at your hostel around midday.

S
Sharon – Australia
July 13, 2026 - Verified booking
The experience of travelling into the Atacama desert & to Salar de Uyuni and seeing the high altitude lakes, geysers, wind sculptured rocks & canyons, the Salvator Dali desert and Isla Incahausi was very special. The driver however had limited knowledge of the area & sometimes gave incorrect information. The accommodation was very basic with no heating in either the rooms or dining room. Apart from two lunches the meals were very ordinary quality & insufficient quantity. Very aware that Bolivia is an impoverished country & food security has recently been an issue given the state of emergency. Tour operator needed to have brought additional food from San Pedro. My advice to fellow vegetarians planning the trip is to bring food!

Amazing experience definitely worth it! The trip includes some of the most beautiful places I’ve ever seen. The drive is long and rough (basically no paved roads) and the hotels are very basic, but it really wasn’t an issue for me. Bring your own towel. Not every hotel has hot water. Just know that you’re not getting luxury and you’ll be fine. Definitely very glad I did this trip.

Ariadne – Germany
July 28, 2026 - Verified booking
My best friend Anna and I thoroughly enjoyed these 4 days in the middle of nowhere catching little to no signal throughout. The shuttle, Border control and stops panned out perfectly. There was always enough food and us vegetarians got given veggie patties etc. Pur driver Carlos made it very memorable by offering Bluetooth in his car which we jammed to the whole ride. Most rides are bumpy but bareable. The hostels have got no warm water or heating so make sure to bring layers, hats and gloves. Toilet paper is a must but you will come across shops for water. Don’t expect anything special at these hostels but enjoy the time with your group and fellow travellers. You’ll survive the night

Once in a lifetime trip! You will never find such a good trip, not only to challenge you out of your comfort zone but also to give you access to some of the most beautiful and remote natural landscape you will ever see. I absolutely recommend this trip to everyone. However, be really aware that it will be really challenging for yourself as you will need to cross the desert, sometimes with more than 4500m of altitude. It is not for the feint of heart. However, be ready for a life changing experience!

April 19, 2026 - Verified booking
I’ve been traveling for a while to know this is one of the best sightseeing experiences in the world, so the review can hardly be bad. I want to give a shout out to “Two Can” Franz, for being our great driver and companion. The best of the tour were obviously the places we’ve been in, the people in our group, and the fact that Franz always gave more time than he said - everywhere. Plus, the creative effort Franz put into the pictures and videos in the Salar. On the negative side, the fact that the hostels are really the minimum you can expect, and you pay for every single extra you can get, some spots that we missed for a variety of reasons, and the return driver who was inexperienced and a bit reckless.
